key_insight: A six-qubit hybrid autoencoder combines quantum Pauli-correlator features with a classical decoder to reconstruct images and run on current IBM quantum hardware.
engineering_relevance: Patchwise MPS compression enables small quantum circuits to process image data, while symmetry averaging makes PCAE2D features exactly equivariant to rotations and reflections.
method: Split images into patches and compress each patch as a matrix product state.
Extract measured features with six-qubit line or grid circuits, then decode using a classical network conditioned on patch position.
Train with a learnable physics-inspired energy term and symmetry-average PCAE2D features.
evidence_signal: Single-image training across six public datasets yielded 25.8–41.6 dB PSNR; five trained models transferred without retraining to IBM hardware and achieved 25.90–31.52 dB.
watch_item: Quantum advantage is not established: the reported unseen-image comparison used formula-based surrogate features, which performed within 1 dB of several simpler classical methods.
paper_title: Hybrid Quantum--Classical Pauli-Correlator Architecture for Image Reconstruction
